{{nihongo|'''Hahaki Shrine'''|波波伎神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Fukuba, {{ill|Kurayoshi, Tottori|ar|كورايوشي (توتوري)|azb|کورایوشی، توتوری|ca|Kurayoshi|ce|Кураёси|ceb|Kurayoshi|cs|Kurajoši (Tottori)|de|Kurayoshi|es|Kurayoshi (Tottori)|et|Kurayoshi|fa|کورایوشی، توتوری|fi|Kurayoshi|fr|Kurayoshi|gl|Kurayoshi|id|Kurayoshi, Tottori|it|Kurayoshi|ja|倉吉市|ko|구라요시시|lt|Kurajošis|mg|Kurayoshi|mzn|کورایوشی، توتوری|nl|Kurayoshi|pl|Kurayoshi|pt|Kurayoshi|ro|Kurayoshi|ru|Кураёси|sv|Kurayoshi|tg|Кураёши|tl|Kurayosyi, Tottori|tok|ma tomo Kulajosi|tr|Kurayoshi|tt|Кураёси|tum|Kurayoshi|uk|Курайоші|ur|کورایوشی، ٹوٹوری|vi|Kurayoshi, Tottori|war|Kurayoshi, Tottori|zh|倉吉市|zh_classical|倉吉市|zh_min_nan|Kurayosi-chhī|zh_yue|倉吉|qid=Q642006}}, {{ill|Tottori Prefecture|Q133935|qid=Q133935}}. It is an Engishiki-listed shrine and its former shrine rank was {{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha}}. {{nihongo|'''Hahaki Shrine'''|波波伎神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hōki Province]].

It enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Yae Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Ame no Wakahiko|Q10940674|qid=Q10940674|lt=Ame-no-Wakahiko-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Shitateruhime|Q11307233|qid=Q11307233|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ca|Sukunabikona|fr|Sukunabikona|it|Sukuna-hikona|ja|スクナビコナ|ko|스쿠나비코나|mni|ꯁꯨꯀꯨꯅꯕꯤꯀꯣꯅ|pl|Sukunabikona|pt|Sukunahikona|simple|Sukunabikona|sv|Suku-Na-Bikona|zh|少彥名|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunabikona-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Takeminakata|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|Q506610|qid=Q506610|lt=Ajisukitakahikone-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|Q11059454|qid=Q11059454|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Tagorihime|Q10932870|qid=Q10932870|lt=Takiribime-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Tagitsuhime|Q10932592|qid=Q10932592|lt=Tagitsuhime-no-Mikoto}}.

== History ==
Its founding period is unclear. The shrine buildings were rebuilt in 1877. In 1916, it merged with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kaita Shrine}}.

== Precincts ==
The sacred grove is a primeval forest of giant {{ill|Castanopsis sieboldii|Q846994|qid=Q846994}} and {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|Q5792073|qid=Q5792073}} trees, with many native camellias. It was designated a natural monument in 1934.

Behind the shrine is the round burial mound called {{ill|Fukuba Kofun|Q63253438|qid=Q63253438}}, considered from the late Kofun period. It was designated a Tottori Prefecture historic site in 1956.
